title: Vanishing of higher bounded Hochschild cohomology
coverage: Read the full LaTeX for all five sections, including the proofs: Thm 2.1 (walk), Lemmas 2.2–2.4, Thm 3.2 (Liouville), Thm 4.1 with Lemmas 4.2–4.5 (rigidity), and Lemmas/Props 5.1–5.4 plus the main proof. Steps I checked by hand: (1) the martingale property of D(W_n)=T(W_n)W_n^*, the L^2 Cauchy estimate, the endpoint lower bound p_a p_b/4 − 18e_h/δ², and the concatenation law (Z_tn, Z_n) for distinct signed blocks; (2) the ultrapower transfer of the bounded-ball 2-continuity modulus; (3) rigidity: that block reductions start and end with positive letters, the coefficient bound 3^L r^{-q/2}, the O(r^{-1/2}) operator-norm discard of repeated indices via Haagerup, the Catalan / free-Poisson moments giving a unitary polar part, and the regularisation x_ε→V; (4) the spectral lemma: ‖(a−b)X‖≤C, the arc inversion with Re H_m ≥ cos(1)h_m, and the trace-weighted sum giving ‖a−b‖_2 ≤ δ_m → 0; (5) the Akemann-type 2-continuity proof (truncation, orthogonal supports, random signs); (6) the Cesàro-averaged cocycle identity, which gives dh=(−1)^k f with sign and indices correct; (7) the conditional-expectation separability removal; (8) the central assembly. Numerical checks: the homotopy identity dJ_z+J_zd=id−cut_z on random cochains over M_2⊕C for n=2,3 (error ~1e-14); the sine-sum bound (sup ≈1.85 ≤ 1+π); the walk parameters n_ℓ=2^{3·2^{ℓ-1}} and the bad-event bounds. Not checked against their sources: the applicability of Popa 2014 Thm 0.1(a) as stated in Lemma 2.2, JKR normal reduction, and classical vanishing without a II_1 summand (CES / Kadison–Ringrose). The paper only uses these as black boxes, and its stated forms look standard.
main_claim: For every complex von Neumann algebra M and k≥2, every bounded Hochschild k-cocycle f: M^k→M is dg for some bounded (k−1)-cochain g, so H_b^k(M,M)=0. Together with Kadison–Sakai this settles the Kadison–Ringrose conjecture positively. The key step is a Liouville theorem for one specially built symmetric random walk on U(M): a bounded map T with bounded-ball 2-continuity and T(x)=E[T(xU)U^*] satisfies T(x)=T(1)x. It is proved by a martingale argument together with a rigidity theorem for free Haar words.
sibling_notes: Family 295's board was empty on arrival. Reusable pieces for companion papers: the central homotopy J_z (verified numerically), the Akemann-style lemma that a normal map is 2-continuous on bounded balls, and the conjugate-function spectral lemma (a bounded S with S(V^k)=aV^k and S(V^{-k})=bV^{-k} forces a=b in a finite algebra). All three check out.
